sentences.text: Shri Dharmendra Gurjar - Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri K. K. Tiwari- G.A. for the State.
ORDER Heard finally, with the consent of the parties.

2] This criminal revision has been filed by the petitioner under Section 438 read with Section 442 of Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 against the order dated 29.01.2025, passed in S.T. No.189/2024, which is being tried against the petitioner and the other accused persons under Sections 376, 328, 506, 323, 201 and 34 of the IPC,
arising out of Crime No.852/2023.

3] In the aforesaid case, an application for exemption from personal appearance was filed by the petitioner and the other accused persons, including the father of the petitioner and his sister, which has been partly allowed in respect of the father and sister of the petitioner, whereas, his application has been rejected on the ground that he appears to be the main accused.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28713 2 CRR-2770-2025 4] Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is a resident of Hyderabad, and is presently employed in D.E.
Shaw India Private Limited as Divisional Manager.
It is also submitted that a false case has been slapped against the petitioner as a counter-blast.

So far as the merits of the case are concerned, it is submitted that the petitioner happens to be the brother-in-law of the prosecutrix's brother, against whom the petitioner's sister has filed a case under Section 498-A of Cr.P.C.

Thus, it is submitted that the impugned order is liable to be set aside and the application filed by the petitioner under Section Piyush Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147294984/
1 228 of B.N.S.S deserves to be allowed.

entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: 5] Counsel for the State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer.

6] Having considered the rival submissions, on perusal of the case- diary, as also the impugned order, it is apparent that the same application has been allowed in respect of the other accused persons, who are the residents of Babina, Jhansi (U.P.), whereas, the petitioner who is a resident Hyderabad, has not been given the benefit of exemption.

In the considered opinion of this Court, when disputed question of facts are involved, and there is no apprehension of the accused running away from the course of justice, the application for exemption could have been allowed liberally.

7] In view of the same, this Court finds that the impugned order dated 29.01.2025 cannot be sustained in the eyes of law, and is accordingly, set aside so far as it relates to the petitioner's prayer for exemption is concerned.

8] Accordingly, the application filed by the petitioner under Section 228 of B.N.S.S. is hereby a l l o w e d , a n d h i s p r e s e n c e i s a l s o e x e m p t e d , a s i n N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-IND:28713 3 CRR-2770-2025 the case of the other accused persons.
9] Needless to say, the petitioner shall mark his presence in the Trial Court as and when directed by the Trial Court to the counsel for the petitioner.
